title: Committee of Supply – Head X (Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head X (Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth)

sections.label: Motion to reduce Head X Estimates
sections.summary: A motion proposes reducing the total sum allocated for Head X of the Estimates by $100.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head X of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sections.label: People queueing to pay respects
sections.summary: People of all races, languages and religions queued in any weather to pay last respects, and Singapore faced SARS in 2003.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: People of all walks of life regarding of race, language or religion came together to queue for hours under the weather, rain or shine, day or night, to pay their last respect.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We faced fear and death together during the 2003 SARS crisis which infected 238 people and killed 33 in Singapore.

sections.label: Proposed Active Arts and Culture credits
sections.summary: MCCY can consider giving all Singaporeans $100 Active Arts and Culture credit, similar to Active SG credits for sports facilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Similar to the $100 Active SG credits for sports facilities, MCCY can consider giving all Singaporeans $100 Active Arts and Culture credit to attend arts and cultural courses or attend local arts & cultural performances.

sections.label: Topping up Active SG credits
sections.summary: Active SG credits should be topped up regularly and expanded to sports events attendance, including SG football leagues and national sports events.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Top up the Active SG credits on a regular basis to promote community sports and expand the use of Active credits to sports events attendance, including our SG football leagues and national sports events.

sections.label: MUIS post-graduate certificate in Islam
sections.summary: MUIS is developing a Post-Graduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Societies to socialise returning graduates to local needs and context.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Health and Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: MUIS is developing Post-Graduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Societies to socialise our returning graduates to our local needs and context.

sections.label: COFA report vision and recommendations
sections.summary: In a report to the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs, COFA proposed a bold vision with 10 key recommendations based on three key thrusts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the report submitted to the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs, COFA proposed a bold vision accompanied by 10 key recommendations based on three key thrusts.

sections.label: Syariah Court divorce applications
sections.summary: Asks how many Syariah Court divorce and counselling applications were received from 2017 to 2019, how many applicants divorced, and the main divorce causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Sir, I would like to ask the Minister how many applications were received by the Syariah Court of Singapore for; firstly divorces, and second, obtaining counselling, between 2017 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And from these applications, how many applicants eventually divorced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, I hope that the Minister can also share three main reasons or factors that are the causes of divorce in the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore within the time period I mentioned earlier.

sections.label: MUIS Appeal Board divorce appeals
sections.summary: Asks how many appeal cases the MUIS Appeal Board receives annually on Syariah Court divorce decisions in 2017, 2018 and 2019, and the main reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How many appeal cases does the MUIS Appeal Board receive annually in relation to the decisions of the Syariah Court of Singapore for divorce cases in 2017, 2018 and 2019, and what are the main reasons for these appeals?

sections.label: MENDAKI preschool learning support
sections.summary: Asks how MENDAKI supports preschool learning for the Malay/Muslim community so children have access to quality education and learning opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How is MENDAKI supporting preschool learning for the Malay/Muslim community to ensure that our children have access to quality education and other learning opportunities?

sections.label: MENDAKI new skills support
sections.summary: Asks how MENDAKI will support the community in gaining new skills to stay relevant and seek employment in new industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can Minister share how will MENDAKI continue to support and encourage the community to explore and gain competencies in new skills, so that they can remain relevant and have the confidence to seek employment in new industries?

sections.label: MUIS madrasah student development plans
sections.summary: Asks what MUIS plans are to ensure madrasahs have resources and capabilities for students' developmental needs in current and new fields.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Investment on our madrasah students’ development is highly important.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to ask what are MUIS' plans to ensure that our madrasahs have the resources and capabilities to fulfil the developmental needs of students in current and new fields?

sections.label: Ciptasama dialogues and MENDAKI education review
sections.summary: Asks about Ciptasama's aim and engagement updates, MENDAKI's plans to review education programmes amid education changes, and possible pre-school sector plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Minister had also mentioned about M3 launching a new series of dialogues, Ciptasama, this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Could the Minister elaborate on the aim of Ciptasama, and provide us with an update on the engagements with our community so far?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some of the changes include an increased number of places for Direct School Admission (DSA), Subject-Based Banding (SBB) in lieu of streaming, the removal of mid-year and year-end examinations for Primary 1 and 2 students, changes to the Primary School Leaving Examinations grade banding, and work readiness initiatives in post-secondary institutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Prior to this, most of MENDAKI's programmes and initiatives often focus on academic excellence and this has resulted in an increase in post-secondary passes, scholarship holders and white collar workers in our community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Now, with a shift towards providing education with multiple pathways to success that is not solely based on academic excellence, as well as collaborations with the industries to ensure work readiness and lifelong learning, MENDAKI's programmes, initiatives and approach must also transform so as to remain relevant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In light of these changes to our education system and landscape as well as schools, what are MENDAKI's plans and progress in reviewing its education programs so as to be in line with these changes that were made to our education system and schools, to ensure that relevant and useful support is given to our community?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Minister for an update on whether MENDAKI has plans to venture into the pre-school sector as well, and whether Mendaki will implement initiatives or programs for this sector, in light of the rapid changes to the pre-school sector in recent years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, last year, during my Hari Raya speech, I said that our Malay/Muslim community is a Community of Success, or in Malay, Masyarakat Gemilang.

sections.label: MUIS mosque fundraising for Courage Fund
sections.summary: Over the past week, MUIS raised money in the mosques to contribute to the Courage Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Over the past week, MUIS raised money in the mosques to contribute to the Courage Fund.

sections.label: Committee on Future Asatizah formed
sections.summary: COFA was formed last year to understand what the community wants in asatizah and how to support the asatizah fraternity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Our asatizah bear significant responsibility in guiding the community on how to thrive in our multicultural society, live in harmony with others and navigate contemporary and future challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This is why we formed the Committee on Future Asatizah (COFA) last year, to better understand what our community would like to see in our asatizah, and in turn, how we can better support the asatizah fraternity.

sections.label: MUIS International Conference on Communities of Success
sections.summary: MUIS will organise an International Conference on Communities of Success later this year to learn from other minority Muslim communities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: There are other minority Muslim communities around the world that share our belief that Muslims can thrive in plural societies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We want to learn from these communities, we want to learn from each other and this is why MUIS will organise an International Conference on Communities of Success later this year.

sections.label: M3 programmes Bersamamu and FITRAH
sections.summary: Through M3 flagship programmes Bersamamu and FITRAH, asatizah volunteers helped close to 3,000 soon-to-wed couples and 40 families with an incarcerated parent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Through M3 flagship programmes like Bersamamu and FITRAH, our asatizah volunteers have helped close to 3,000 soon-to-wed couples as well as 40 families where at least one parent is incarcerated.

sections.label: Asatizah Workforce Development Plan
sections.summary: MUIS has developed the Asatizah Workforce Development Plan, which Senior Minister of State Maliki will elaborate on later.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To facilitate this transformation, MUIS has developed the Asatizah Workforce Development Plan (AWDP), on which Senior Minister of State Maliki will elaborate later.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim students' educational progress
sections.summary: In 1980, 16% of Malay/Muslim students achieved five GCE O level passes; today the proportion is four times that, and nine in 10 make it to post-secondary education.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In 1980, only 16% of Malay/Muslim students achieved five GCE "O" level passes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: By the end of the decade, we doubled the proportion of Malay/Muslim students who achieved five GCE "O" Level Passes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Today, this proportion is four times that in 1980.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Today, nine in 10 of Malay/Muslim students in a P1 cohort make it to University, Polytechnic, ITE or other post-Secondary education institutes.

sections.label: Investing in asatizah and youth
sections.summary: The passage states commitment to enhance asatizah competencies, support children and youth educationally, and work with the Malay/Muslim community for Singapore's future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As our asatizah shape the community’s character and identity, we must be committed in our investment to enhance our asatizah’s competencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will also invest in the future of our children and youth by providing educational support to develop a future generation that is competent and capable in contributing back to society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: And we are determined to work together with the Malay/Muslim community, not just to build a Community of Success, but also to build a prosperous future together for Singapore.

sections.label: Committee on Future Asatizah formed
sections.summary: The Committee on Future Asatizah was formed in March 2019 and held 16 engagement sessions over nine months with over 1,900 stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In March 2019, we formed the Committee on Future Asatizah (COFA) and I led the engagements on the vision for future asatizah.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The diversity reflects the expanded role expected of future asatizah.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We held 16 engagements sessions over nine months, involving over 1,900 stakeholders.

sections.label: COFA strategic thrusts and AWDP
sections.summary: COFA proposed three strategic thrusts, and MUIS is developing an Asatizah Workforce Development Plan to professionalise the sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: COFA proposed to realise the vision through three strategic thrusts: first, we will professionalise the asatizah sector; second, we will strengthen key religious institutions; and third, we will do more to nurture inspiring asatizah.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To transform and professionalise the sector, I am glad to share that MUIS is developing an Asatizah Workforce Development Plan (AWDP) to enhance the attractiveness of the religious sector and the skills and competencies of our asatizah.

sections.label: Bersamamu training for Kadis
sections.summary: ROMM has worked with MSF to train Kadis and Naib Kadis to support soon-to-wed couples, and Bersamamu has benefited close to 3,000 couples since July 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, to further enhance Bersamamu, ROMM has been working closely with MSF to train Kadis and Naib Kadis to better engage and support soon-to-wed couples.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Thus far, Bersamamu has benefited close to 3,000 couples since its launch in July 2019.

sections.label: Asatizah as religious thought leaders
sections.summary: The asatizah role has evolved to religious leaders, with a long-term vision to develop future cohorts as religious thought leaders locally and internationally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The role of an asatizah has evolved from only functioning as religious teachers to religious leaders who contribute their expertise in the religious and non-religious sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Our long-term vision is to develop our future cohorts of asatizah as religious thought leaders who are highly regarded locally and internationally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Chairman, our young asatizah can be great assets to the community, beyond the mosque and the madrasah.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We must continue to invest in their development.

sections.label: MENDAKI MUIS Preschool Grant
sections.summary: MENDAKI and MUIS set up the MENDAKI MUIS Preschool Grant to provide additional financial support for low-income parents, with amounts doubled to $60 and $120.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: While initiatives, such as the Preschool Outreach Programme, have paid off, there are vulnerable families in our community who need extra support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Thus, MENDAKI and MUIS have set up the MENDAKI MUIS Preschool Grant (MMPG) which builds on existing Government initiatives to provide additional financial support for our low-income parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MMPG will double that amount to $60 and the Government’s CDA co-matching initiative will double the $60 to $120 a month.

sections.label: MENDAKI Tuition Scheme centres
sections.summary: MTS and MOE's UPLIFT help students needing extra coaching, with over 7,500 enrolled in 85 MTS centres and 15 more planned next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As our children progress into schools, MENDAKI Tuition Scheme (MTS) and MOE's UPLIFT programme step in to help those who need extra coaching and motivation to attend school more regularly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This year, so far, more than 7,500 students have enrolled in our 85 MTS centres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: By next year, we intend to introduce 15 more centres to make it 100.

sections.label: MENDAKI SENSE jobseekers
sections.summary: MENDAKI SENSE has helped over 2,000 Malay jobseekers find employment through its programmes in the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MENDAKI SENSE has also helped over 2,000 Malay jobseekers who come to its doors to find employment through their programmes in the last five years and we will continue to strengthen its efforts.

sections.label: MMPG grant for families
sections.summary: MMPG helps families with children six and below by quadrupling CDA savings for pre-school fees, medical expenses, enrichment and glasses, applied through MENDAKI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: MMPG will help families with children who are six years old and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The grant can be used to quadruple their CDA savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This money can be used for the pre-school fees, medical expenses, enrichment programmes and even prescriptive glasses for their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, for Malay/Muslim families with a per capita income (PCI) of $650 and families with children who are six years old and below, they can apply through MENDAKI.

sections.label: Revamped programmes and MTS restructuring
sections.summary: Community feedback led to revamped programmes, with MTS centres restructured and Cluster Principals introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: From there, we obtained all kinds of feedback from the community and we have revamped our programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We will restructure the MTS centres and introduce Cluster Principals.

sections.label: UNESCO inscriptions and nominations
sections.summary: The Singapore Botanic Gardens was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015, and in 2019 nomination documents were submitted for Hawker Culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: In 2015, the Singapore Botanic Gardens was successfully inscribed as Singapore's first UNESCO World Heritage Site and in 2019, we submitted the nomination documents to have "Hawker Culture in Singapore: Community Dining and Culinary Practices in a Multicultural Urban Context" on the UNESCO's Representative List.

sections.label: 2019 SEA Games results
sections.summary: The 2019 SEA Games brought Team Singapore mixed results, including first softball gold and underwater hockey sweep, but no water-polo gold for 50 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: The 2019 SEA Games was a mixed-bag of results for Team Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: While we had a number of hits, such as winning our first-ever gold in softball and making a clean gold medal sweep in underwater hockey, we also had a number of misses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: For the first time in 50 years, we did not win a gold for water-polo and did not do as well as we thought we would in women's table tennis doubles.

sections.label: SG Youth Action Plan launch
sections.summary: The Ministry and National Youth Council launched the SG Youth Action Plan to let youths shape Singapore's 2025 vision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Last year, the Ministry and the National Youth Council (NYC) launched the SG Youth Action Plan, an ambitious effort to envision the future of Singapore in 2025 and provide a platform for Singapore's youths to shape their vision for the country, develop plans for youth, community organisations, businesses and the Government to realise this vision together.

sections.label: Our Singapore Fund introduction
sections.summary: At Budget 2016 the Government introduced Our Singapore Fund to support active citizens solving ground problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, at Budget 2016, the Government introduced Our Singapore Fund to encourage and support active citizens that are taking the initiative to solve ground problems, strengthen community spirit and contribute to nation-building.

sections.label: SG Cares Volunteer Centres rollout
sections.summary: MCCY rolled out SG Cares Volunteer Centres in seven towns to grow and coordinate volunteer supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Last year, MCCY rolled out SG Cares Volunteer Centres in seven towns to grow and coordinate volunteer supply, facilitate partnerships between community partners and build capabilities in these towns.

sections.label: Grant funding framework suggestions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would increase maximum funding and revise grant disbursement for longer-term projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of the $250 million top-up and the spirit of Singapore Together, would the Ministry consider the following.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, increasing the maximum funding in Our Singapore Fund and other funds to minimise the need to apply for multiple grants by ground-ups who are made up of citizen volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, revising the framework in disbursing grants such that projects which are longer-term in nature or design, for example research, or projects which are seeking to be more sustainable, can receive longer term funding required in line with the time required for community development.

sections.label: LGBTQ+ social harmony engagement
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would convene community engagement initiatives bridging religious groups, the LGBTQ+ community and others.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2019 IPS study found that there have been "steep drops" in opposition towards LGBTQ+ issues.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If these divisions were left unchecked, it increases the potential for acts of violence and discrimination to be committed against vulnerable groups, including hate speech and online harassment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of the friction concerning LGBTQ+ issues, one way to foster social harmony would be to include vulnerable and marginalised groups, such as the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities and migrant workers and other groups, to be a mainstay in initiatives similar to IRCCs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The purpose of such initiatives is not to convert anyone to any particular viewpoint on these issues, but to mitigate polarisation by strengthening social cohesion and fostering understanding and respect across differences.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the contributions of IRCCs in promoting social harmony, could the Ministry convene similar community engagement initiatives that aim to bridge gaps between religious groups, the LGBTQ+ community and other stakeholders, with the aim of fostering mutual understanding?

sections.label: Disability Sports Master Plan implementation
sections.summary: The Disability Sports Master Plan, or DSMP, began implementation in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Disability Sports Master Plan, otherwise known as the DSMP, started its implementation in 2016.

sections.label: Disability sports participation recommendations
sections.summary: The DSMP's 2015 research identified barriers and made three recommendations on access, capabilities and public awareness for disability sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After research done in 2015, the DSMP had identified the barriers to participation and had three broad recommendations then; which was to expand access and opportunities for sports participation by PWDs, develop organisational and professional capabilities in disability sports, and build public awareness of disability sports and strengthen affinity with Team Singapore athletes.

sections.label: Inclusive gyms and pool wheelchairs
sections.summary: There are seven inclusive gyms and pool wheelchairs at five ActiveSG pools with ramps into the pools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently there are seven inclusive gyms and pool wheelchairs have been put in place at five Active SG pools where there are ramps into the pools.

sections.label: Students with disabilities in PE
sections.summary: The passage asks how many students with disabilities are still not participating in PE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How many students with disabilities are still not participating in PE?

sections.label: Community Chest funding excludes sports
sections.summary: A Community Chest Charity Support Fund call made programmes for psycho-socio well-being eligible but excluded sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An example is a recent Community Chest Charity Support Fund call, where it was informed that "agencies that support programmes that contribute to the psycho-socio well-being of target clients" would be eligible for funding, but such programmes would exclude "sports".

sections.label: Mind Matters mental health programme
sections.summary: Mind Matters, created in 2017, reached only 55 participants in five full sessions, prompting a question on mental health support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The programme, Mind Matters, was created in 2017 to develop the mental health framework but the reach in this programme has been very limited with only five full sessions being conducted to 55 participants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider providing mental health support as a strategic priority, and clarify what measures are in place for current and retiring athletes in this regard?

sections.label: Sponsorship matching and World Cup goal
sections.summary: The passage discusses One Team Singapore matching donations but not sponsorships, and asks about FAS plans for FIFA World Cup 2034.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While such sponsorships may be geared towards high performance, the One Team Singapore funding mechanism only allows donations to be matched and not sponsorships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This regulation appears to penalise the NSA for their efforts, rather than the sponsor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If the concern is sponsors receiving "double" benefit through "doubled" recognition for the matched funds, can this be mitigated by imposing a condition on the matched funds, rather than rejecting such matching altogether?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If this Fund can apply to sponsorships as well, it can encourage corporates to play a bigger part in supporting local sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: I asked MCCY what are the Football Association of Singapore (FAS)'s plans in working towards achieving this goal for Singapore's Football National Team to qualify for FIFA World Cup in 2034.

sections.label: Sports industry GDP growth
sections.summary: Sports industry GDP contribution grew from $300 million in 2000 to $1 billion in 2008, including several hosted events.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: GDP contribution from the sports industry grew from $300 million in 2000 to $1 billion in 2008, including the hosting of the 2005 International Olympic Committee Session, 2008 inaugural F1 Singapore Grand Prix, 2009 inaugural Asian Youth Games, and 2010 inaugural Youth Olympic Games (YOG).

sections.label: Sports industry target and staff exodus
sections.summary: A 2008 target of $2 billion GDP and 20,000 jobs by 2015 was announced, while staff exodus occurred.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2008, the former MCYS Minister, Dr Vivian Balakrishnan, announced a target for the Singapore sports industry: $2 billion annual contribution to Singapore’s GDP and the creation of 20,000 jobs by 2015.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Instead, we have witnessed a continuous exodus of staff last year and this year, including the majority C-suite of SportsHub: CEO, CFO, COO, Chief Commercial Officer, and General Counsel.

sections.label: SportsHub sporting event days promise
sections.summary: It asks for an update on keeping the sporting calendar vibrant given SportsHub's non-performance of its 90 event days promise.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Please also update how we will keep our sporting calendar vibrant, given the non-performance of the contractual promise by SportsHub Private Limited to host 90 sporting event days per year at National Stadium.

sections.label: Relief measures for arts groups
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government will consider a 1:2 matching grant and more project and production grant funding for arts groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, can the Government consider launching a Relief and Recovery Measures to Arts Group by providing 1:2 matching grant instead of 1:1?

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, will the Government also consider providing more for the project and production grant, such as the Tote Board Arts Fund so as to allow the arts groups to work on recovery plans to bring back audiences and call back artistes for future performances?

sections.label: Review of CMF disbursement
sections.summary: It hopes the Government will review CMF disbursement by increasing the ratio to 1:2 and increasing project and production grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To help arts groups tide over this difficult period, I hope the Government can review the disbursement of CMF by: First, the Government can consider launching a relief package to help arts groups overcome the current difficulties by increasing the ratio of CMF from 1:1 to 1:2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, the Government can consider increasing project and production grants for arts groups, so that they can come up with exciting programmes to attract audiences.

sections.label: Rental rebates for arts groups
sections.summary: It asks whether the National Arts Council can provide rental rebates for arts groups at venues such as Goodman Arts Centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, can the National Arts Council help provide rental rebates, for arts group housed at Goodman Arts Centre and Stamford Arts Centre, to name a few.

sections.label: Arts groups space and rental rebates
sections.summary: A speaker asks for inter-Ministerial discussions on more arts space and rental rebates for arts groups during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   As arts groups grow, they will need more space for practice, rehearsals, and storing props and stage sets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With limited land space in Singapore, there are not many places that can be used for arts groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope we could do the following: First, Government Ministries can engage in inter-Ministerial discussions on how to increase space allocated for culture and arts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, during the current COVID-19 outbreak, I hope that we can consider granting rental rebates to arts groups, so that they can focus on rehearsals as usual, and not lose the drive to perform due to loss of income because of cancellation of performances.

sections.label: WeCare Arts Fund and attendance
sections.summary: The WeCare Arts Fund supports artists and Social Service Agencies, and non-ticketed arts attendance reached an all-time high in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One example is the WeCare Arts Fund, a year-round funding scheme that supports artists and Social Service Agencies in developing participatory workshops for beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In fact, non-ticketed arts attendance has been climbing over the years, reaching an all-time high in 2018.

sections.label: Gillman Barracks awareness and tenants

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, anecdotally, the awareness of Gillman Barracks is not high and the tenants there are not doing well as a result.

sections.label: Heartbeat arts and crafts workshops
sections.summary: Since opening two years ago, Heartbeat has held more than 250 workshops on arts and crafts, painting, sculpturing and calligraphy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Since its opening two years ago, Heartbeat has held more than 250 workshops on arts and crafts, painting, sculpturing, calligraphy.

sections.label: Team Singapore SEA Games medals
sections.summary: Team Singapore athletes at the SEA Games brought home 53 gold, 46 silver and 68 bronze medals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our country rallied behind Team Singapore athletes at the SEA Games, who brought home 53 gold medals, 46 silver medals and 68 bronze medals.

sections.label: Hawker Culture UNESCO nomination

sentences.text: With strong public support, we submitted our nomination to inscribe Hawker Culture in Singapore on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

sections.label: Pre-school movement skills programme
sections.summary: After partnering 125 pre-schools and reaching over 5,000 children last year, the programme will be doubled to 250 pre-schools this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Last year, we partnered 125 pre-schools and introduced fundamental movement skills such as jumping, throwing and balancing in a safe and fun way to more than 5,000 children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This year, we will double efforts, and make this available to 250 pre-schools.

sections.label: Singapore Philatelic Museum revamp
sections.summary: The Singapore Philatelic Museum will be revamped as a dedicated children's museum with interactive and immersive exhibits on themes including Singapore and regional heritage and culture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Singapore Philatelic Museum will be revamped as a dedicated children’s museum where children can learn about a wide range of themes, including the heritage and culture of Singapore and the region, by playing with interactive and immersive exhibits.

sections.label: Museum-based Learning for students
sections.summary: In 2020 the National Heritage Board will introduce Museum-based Learning in MOE's Learning Journeys, with Primary 6 and Secondary 2 cohorts visiting the Asian Civilisations Museum and National Museum of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In 2020, the National Heritage Board will introduce Museum-based Learning (MBL) as part of MOE's Learning Journeys for students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: All Primary 6 and Secondary 2 cohorts will visit the Asian Civilisations Museum and National Museum of Singapore respectively.

sections.label: Asia-Ready Exposure Programme immersion
sections.summary: The National Youth Council will partner IHLs to expand short-term immersion to ASEAN, China and India through the Asia-Ready Exposure Programme, supporting up to 10,000 youths yearly by 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The National Youth Council (NYC) will partner IHLs to expand short-term immersion opportunities to ASEAN, China and India for ITE, Polytechnic and University students, through the new Asia-Ready Exposure Programme (AEP).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: By 2022, NYC's regional exposure programmes, including the AEP, will support up to 10,000 youths each year.

sections.label: Free gyms and pools for seniors
sections.summary: From this year, public gyms and swimming pools will be free for all Singaporeans aged 65 years and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: From this year, we will make public gyms and swimming pools free for all Singaporeans aged 65 years and above.

sections.label: WeCare Arts Fund enhancement
sections.summary: The enhanced WeCare Arts Fund will launch WeCare Arts Experiences with the five CDCs, giving less privileged families free ticketed presentations via subsidies of up to $40, aiming to reach 20,000 beneficiaries and volunteers by 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This year, we will enhance the WeCare Arts Fund by launching the WeCare Arts Experiences, in partnership with the five Community Development Councils (CDCs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This will enable less privileged families to attend ticketed presentations for free at our cultural institutions such as the Esplanade, SSO and NHB museums, through a subsidy of up to $40 for a ticket.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: By 2022, the National Arts Council and CDCs aim to reach up to 20,000 beneficiaries and volunteers under the scheme.

sections.label: SG Youth Action Plan
sections.summary: Over 70,000 youths shared ideas and views on Singapore in 2025 through the SG Youth Action Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: A clear manifestation of this has been the crafting of the SG Youth Action Plan, where more than 70,000 youths proactively shared their ideas and views on Singapore in 2025.

sections.label: Funding for active citizenry
sections.summary: Government is prepared to invest up to $175 million to 2025, with $20 million into Our Singapore Fund extended to SG60.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Finance Minister has shared in his Budget Speech that the Government is prepared to invest up to $175 million from now to 2025 to engage active citizenry and develop partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To support more projects, we will put $20 million of these funds into Our Singapore Fund and extend it to SG60 in 2025.

sections.label: Youth platforms for differences
sections.summary: Youth Conversations and SG Youth Action Plan gave youths a safe space to express views, including on LGBTQ issues, with civility and respect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: It is grounded on personal values and beliefs and consensus is not always possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: However, we agree with Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, that we do not shy away from discussing it and it is important that we have platforms where we can engage on our differences on the basis of mutual respect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For instance, at the Youth Conversations and SG Youth Action Plan engagements, youths had a safe space to express views, on their aspirations, concerns, fears and disappointments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Participants voiced their opinions, including on LGBTQ issues, while others listened with civility and respect.

sections.label: Scoot and MFA courage
sections.summary: Scoot pilots and crew and MFA officers who flew to Wuhan to retrieve Singaporeans showed courage, duty and self-sacrifice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Some, like the pilots and crew of Scoot and the MFA officers who flew into Wuhan to retrieve Singaporeans there, showed courage, sense of duty and self-sacrifice, and made the nation proud.

sections.label: Mask distribution without queues
sections.summary: Singapore distributed four masks per household within days, without queues, unlike other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: While other countries see their citizens standing in line in the cold for hours for two pieces of masks per person, we have distributed four masks per household within days, without queues.

sections.label: SG United portal
sections.summary: SG United was introduced as a one-stop portal to volunteer, donate, start and share community-led initiatives in response to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We are heartened by such initiatives, and want to inspire more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This is why we introduced SG United, a one-stop portal to volunteer, donate, start and share community-led initiatives in response to COVID-19.

sections.label: SG Youth Action Plan launch
sections.summary: The SG Youth Action Plan was launched last May, reaching over 400,000 youths and engaging close to 70,000 through digital engagement, roadshows and focus groups.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Last May, we launched a national platform for youths to articulate and achieve their vision for Singapore in 2025: the SG Youth Action Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Since SG Youth Action Plan’s launch, we reached out to over 400,000 youths, and engaged close to 70,000 of them through digital engagement, public roadshows and focus group discussions.

sections.label: YAC Summit team funding
sections.summary: Top teams will present proposals at the YAC Summit next month for up to $50,000 of funding, while NYC helps all 57 teams implement their ideas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: While the top teams will present their proposals at the YAC Summit next month for up to $50,000 of funding, NYC will help all 57 teams to implement their ideas.

sections.label: TAFEP mental health job advice
sections.summary: Following feedback, TAFEP has advised employers against asking job applicants about mental health history when there is no relevance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Following such feedback, TAFEP has taken steps to advise employers against asking job applicants about their mental health history when there is no relevance.

sections.label: Youth vision and proposals
sections.summary: The SG Youth Action Plan gathered youth voices into a statement of values and 57 proposals, with top 12 teams to pitch at the YAC Summit in April.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In May 2019, we launched "SG Youth Action Plan" for youth to articulate their vision for Singapore in 2025 and to take action to achieve that vision.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We reached out to over 400,000 youths and engaged 70,000 more closely, compiling thousands of youth voices into a clear statement on what young people hope to see in Singapore in the near future: a society that embodies the values of inclusiveness, fairness, care, sustainability and progress.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The youth teams have come up with 57 exciting proposals on the themes of environment, societal issues, and jobs and future of work, and I look forward to seeing the top 12 teams pitch their proposals at the YAC Summit in April.

sections.label: RSVP senior volunteering MOU
sections.summary: Under the MOU, RSVP aims to reach 30,000 seniors in its first year and match them to suitable volunteering opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: With the MOU, RSVP aims to reach out to 30,000 seniors in its first year and match them to suitable volunteering opportunities.

sections.label: New centre appointments this year

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Last year, four were established in Kreta Ayer, Toa Payoh, Boon Lay and Woodlands.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This year, eight others will be appointed at Ang Mo Kio, Bukit Merah, Choa Chu Kang, Clementi, Geylang, Jalan Besar, Tampines and Yishun.

sections.label: Inclusive and senior-friendly gyms
sections.summary: The DSMP's three thrusts remain relevant; eight inclusive gyms exist, three more will be retrofitted yearly, and all ActiveSG gyms will be inclusive by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The three key thrusts of the DSMP remain relevant and we are making progress on its recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We currently have eight inclusive and senior-friendly gyms with equipment suitable for use by all, including PWDs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: SportSG plans to retrofit three more gyms each year over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: By 2026, all ActiveSG gyms in Singapore will be inclusive and senior-friendly.

sections.label: Communities of Care grant

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We are disbursing $600,000 to support 18 community projects and 31 SportCares bursary recipients this year.

sections.label: Bicentennial Community Fund matching
sections.summary: Donations to Institutions of a Public Character will continue to be matched via the Bicentennial Community Fund until December 2020, from March 2020 previously.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Donations to Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs) will continue to be matched via the Bicentennial Community Fund until December 2020, from March 2020 previously.

sections.label: Arts and culture sector support
sections.summary: MCCY will set aside around $1.6 million for the arts and culture sector, with a new 30% venue rental subsidy and a grant open from 16 March.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: MCCY will therefore set aside around $1.6 million to support the arts and culture sector and to prepare the sector for the post-disease recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: MCCY will provide a new 30% subsidy for venue rental and associated costs at our national cultural institutions. including the Esplanade, Arts House Limited venues, and the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This subsidy will be for arts and culture activities, including productions and workshops taking place from 7 March, tomorrow, to 30 June.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The grant will be open for application from 16 March and will subsidise local courses and programmes.

sections.label: Sports industry GDP and events
sections.summary: The sports industry's GDP contribution reached $1.7 billion in 2018, and the Singapore Sports Hub hosted 212 events last year.

sentences.text: The GDP contribution of the sports industry has grown steadily, reaching $1.7 billion in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Singapore Sports Hub hosted 212 events last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Regarding the acquisition of majority stakeholder InfraRed Capital Partners by Sun Life, we recently sought clarification from Sports Hub Private Limited (SHPL) and we have obtained their assurance that this will not have any direct impact on the Sports Hub operations.

sections.label: Southeast Asian Games athletes
sections.summary: The speaker attended the 30th Southeast Asian Games in the Philippines, where 659 athletes achieved more than 50 gold medals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Twenty-nineteen was a busy year for our athletes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: I attended the 30th Southeast Asian Games in the Philippines where we fielded 659 athletes and achieved more than 50 gold medals.

sections.label: Cultural Matching Fund donations
sections.summary: Since 2013, the Cultural Matching Fund has benefited over 100 arts and heritage charities through one-for-one matching to over $215 million of private donations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Since it was set up in 2013, the Cultural Matching Fund has benefited over 100 arts and heritage charities through one-for-one matching to over $215 million of private donations.

sections.label: NAC stART Fund plan

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Over the coming three years till 2022, NAC plans to build the stART Fund to $10 million, which aims to support about 100 arts groups.

sections.label: Temasek Foundation Inspire Fund athletes
sections.summary: The Government set aside $50 million to match cash donations, and with Temasek Foundation support, $100,000 will be set aside annually for a Temasek Foundation Inspire Fund for Athletes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The Government has set aside $50 million to match cash donations to encourage more to step forward.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: But we are mindful that there are athletes outside the high performance sports system such as our indoor skydivers, national dodgeball and tchoukball squads who have done well in internationally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: So, with support from Temasek Foundation, $100,000 will be set aside annually for a Temasek Foundation Inspire Fund for Athletes that will provide campaign funding for such athletes.

sections.label: Street Corner Heritage Galleries
sections.summary: The Government will partner local shop owners within Singapore's historic precincts to co-create Street Corner Heritage Galleries highlighting heritage in neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Beyond shared stories, traditions and practices that are passed on from generation to generation, our heritage is also embodied in historical buildings and neighbourhood icons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will partner local shop owners within Singapore's historic precincts to co-create Street Corner Heritage Galleries and highlight heritage right in our neighbourhoods.

sections.label: Balestier first heritage precinct
sections.summary: Balestier will be the first precinct, with five Street Corner Heritage Galleries opening to the public from tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)

sections.label: Street Corner Heritage Galleries precincts
sections.summary: By 2022, Street Corner Heritage Galleries will exist in Kampong Gelam, Kreta Ayer, Little India and Geylang Serai.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: By 2022, there will be Street Corner Heritage Galleries in four other historic precincts – Kampong Gelam, Kreta Ayer, Little India and Geylang Serai.

sections.label: Stewards of Intangible Cultural Heritage Award
sections.summary: The inaugural Stewards of Singapore's Intangible Cultural Heritage Award this year aims to acknowledge recipients' contributions and encourage safeguarding and transmitting intangible cultural heritage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Through the inaugural Stewards of Singapore's Intangible Cultural Heritage Award which will be held this year, we hope to acknowledge the recipients' contributions and encourage them to continue safeguarding and transmitting intangible cultural heritage in their respective fields to the next generation.

sections.label: Yishun Sports Complex budget question
sections.summary: The question asks what the budget is for the Yishun Sports Complex project.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: My question is: what is budget for this Yishun Sports Complex project.

sections.label: Sports Hub value-for-money question
sections.summary: The question asks whether the national icon is value-for-money given the monthly unitary payment to Sports Hub Private Limited versus its contractual performance and ability to meet expectations.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: It was developed with EDB, STB and so on.

sections.label: National E-sports Association setup
sections.summary: Among new developments in sports such as e-sports, the National E-sports Association was recently set up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: There are many new interesting developments in sports, like we mentioned e-sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We have recently set up the National E-sports Association.

sections.label: ActiveSG Credit age 65
sections.summary: The age of 65 was chosen for free ActiveSG admission as it coincides with retirement age and more free time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The second question about Active SG Credit, we had hoped the free admission will have addressed the Member's request.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: But I think why 65 – we thought that is a good age, timing with how we see our lives, getting into retirement age and having more time on your hands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: It is really a good time to get into an active lifestyle and we hope that ActiveSG gym and swimming pool will be part of the lives of those 65 and above.

sections.label: Somerset Belt master plan

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: On the Somerset Belt, last year we went through a long process, engaging many youths on developing a master plan for the Somerset Belt as a place where youths can gather, realise their aspirations.

sections.label: OSF fund low hurdles
sections.summary: OSF is structured with low hurdles and low amounts to encourage as many ground-up projects and groups as possible, and MCCY is harmonising grant rules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Having said that, OSF is a fund that will encourage as many ground-up projects and groups as much as possible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, the structure is set low, with low hurdles so that it is easy to get but the amount generally is kept low – for a purpose because we want to encourage as many as possible to access the funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: MCCY is also in the process of harmonising the rules of the grants.

sentences.text: Goal 2034 is a goal set by FAS.
